name: cold_winter_workday
description: Cold winter workday with high heating-driven electricity load. This is the dominant high-load regime in the dataset. Sub-zero temperatures drive electric heating demand, creating a characteristic dual-peak pattern: a morning ramp-up as factories and offices open (8-10am), a mild midday dip, and a strong evening peak (17-20pm) as residential heating combines with cooking and lighting. Load stays elevated overnight due to continuous heating.
reasoning: Winter workdays consistently produce the highest load in this dataset (5000-5600 MW vs. dataset mean of ~2400 MW). The key drivers are: (1) sub-zero skin temperatures requiring electric heating, (2) industrial/commercial activity on workdays, (3) the combination of heating + industrial load that only occurs on winter workdays. This prototype captures the single most important regime for accurate forecasting.

Skin_temperature.reasoning: Sub-zero temperatures are the primary driver of heating demand. Global stats show p25=-0.48°C, so this captures roughly the coldest quarter of the data.

solar_month.reasoning: Winter months. Lunar calendar is less reliable for seasonal filtering.

is_workday.reasoning: Workdays have industrial + commercial + residential load stacked together.

is_holiday.reasoning: Exclude holidays (including Spring Festival) which drastically reduce industrial load even in winter.

Relative_humidity.reasoning: No requirement — humidity has weak correlation with load in winter.

Total_precipitation_4h_ahead.reasoning: No requirement — precipitation has minimal impact on heating-driven load.

Surface_net_solar_radiation.reasoning: No requirement — solar radiation is low in winter regardless.

10_metre_wind.reasoning: No requirement — wind has secondary effect compared to temperature.

day_of_week.reasoning: No requirement beyond is_workday — weekday variation is minimal within workdays.

pricing.reasoning: No requirement — pricing tier doesn't drive the load pattern shape.

expected_load_characteristics.description: High overall load with dual-peak daily pattern (morning industrial + evening residential)
